# Configuration

`esp-tinybft` has two configuration layers. **Compile-time configuration** is set via ESP-IDF Kconfig (`Kconfig.projbuild` at the component root, surfaced in the host project's `sdkconfig.defaults` and `sdkconfig`); every option is consumed by `src/tbft_config.h` and feeds a set of `_Static_assert` checks. **Runtime configuration** is a plain-text file on SPIFFS parsed by `parse_config()` in `src/tbft_libbyz.c:96`; the format is line-based and the parser auto-detects the transport flavour (UDP vs ESP-NOW) by checking whether the second field contains a `:`. Public keys are DER-encoded and live alongside the config file; the local private key is passed separately as a path argument to `Byz_init_replica()` / `Byz_init_client()`.

## Overview

The two layers are deliberately decoupled. The Kconfig options (defaults listed below) set the **maximums** the static protocol buffers are sized for at compile time. The runtime config file sets the **actuals** for a particular cluster: how many replicas, which keys, which IP or MAC, which timeouts. The parser enforces `3f+1 ≤ num_nodes ≤ TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:121-132`) and `1 ≤ f ≤ TBFT_MAX_FAULTY` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:114-118`), so a misconfigured file fails fast at `Byz_init_replica` time rather than silently truncating the certificate quorums at runtime.

## Kconfig options

All options are defined in `Kconfig.projbuild` at the component root. Defaults are the values used when the option is not explicitly set in `sdkconfig` or `sdkconfig.defaults`.

| Symbol | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CONFIG_TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | int | 1440 | 256–4096 | Maximum message size in bytes. Multiple of 8 (assert enforced). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_MAX_REPLY_SIZE` | int | 1136 | — | Maximum reply payload (1136 = 1440 − 48 hdr − 256 sig). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_BLOCK_SIZE` | int | 1024 | 16–4096 | State page/block size in bytes. Power of 2. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS` | int | 4 | 4–32 | Maximum replicas supported. Drives authenticator size and static buffers. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE` | int | 16 | 4–64 | In-flight sequence numbers. Power of 2 and > `CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL`. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL` | int | 8 | 1–32 | Sequence numbers between checkpoints. < `WINDOW_SIZE`. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS` | int | 1 | 1–16 | Maximum simultaneous clients. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS` | int | 256 | — | Maximum state blocks (`state_size / BLOCK_SIZE`). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_RQUEUE_MAX` | int | 8 | 4–256 | Request queue depth (×2 queues, each `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_NDET_BUF_SIZE` | int | 256 | 32–4096 | Non-deterministic choices buffer. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_P_LEVELS` | int | 4 | 2–8 | Merkle partition tree depth. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_ANTI_REPLAY_WINDOW_MS` | int | 30000 | — | Anti-replay window in milliseconds. `0` disables. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_DISABLE_MULTICAST` | bool | n | — | Use unicast UDP for all sends. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_TRANSPORT_TYPE` | choice | `TBFT_TRANSPORT_UDP` | UDP / ESP-NOW | Transport backend. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_ESPNOW_SEND_TASK_PRIORITY` | int | 5 | — | FreeRTOS priority of the ESP-NOW send task (must match `Byz_replica_run()` priority). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_ESPNOW_TX_CREDITS` | int | 6 | 2–12 | Concurrent ESP-NOW send slots. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_PRINT_STATS` | bool | n | — | Compile in stats counters. |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_VIEW_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_US` | int | 5000000 | 1M–60M | Default view-change period (5 s). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_US` | int | 1000000 | 100k–30M | Status broadcast period (1 s). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_US` | int | 2500000 | 100k–30M | State fetch / recovery period (2.5 s). |
| `CONFIG_TBFT_CLIENT_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS` | int | 10000 | 1k–120k | Client reply timeout (10 s). |

The choice `TBFT_TRANSPORT_TYPE` has two values:

| Value | Selects | Extra `select`s | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TBFT_TRANSPORT_UDP` | UDP (lwIP sockets) | `LWIP_IP4_REASSEMBLY`, `LWIP_IP4_FRAG` | Standard UDP over IP; supports multicast (unless `TBFT_DISABLE_MULTICAST`). |
| `TBFT_TRANSPORT_ESPNOW` | ESP-NOW v2.0 | — | 1470-byte packet cap with auto-fragmentation. Host app must call `esp_wifi_init()`. |

The example projects override most of these in their `sdkconfig.defaults`:

| File | Cluster | `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS` | `WINDOW_SIZE` | `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | Transport |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/counter/sdkconfig.defaults` | 7 replicas + 1 client (f=2) | 7 | 4 | 2048 | ESP-NOW |
| `examples/simple_wallet/sdkconfig.defaults` | 3 replicas + 1 client (f=1) | 4 (default) | 16 | 1248 | ESP-NOW (unicast) |

The counter example uses `CONFIG_TBFT_MAX_STATE_BLOCKS=8` and `CONFIG_TBFT_P_LEVELS=2` because the app state is tiny (a single `int`); the simple_wallet example uses the same. Both enable `CONFIG_LWIP_IP4_FRAG=y` and `CONFIG_LWIP_IP4_REASSEMBLY=y` for UDP large messages (e.g. New_key on first boot) and disable the idle-task WDT (`CONFIG_ESP_TASK_WDT_CHECK_IDLE_TASK_CPU0=n`) because `replica_task` / `client_task` cooperatively feed the watchdog on the single-core ESP32-C3.

## Derived constants

`src/tbft_config.h:80-105` derives a number of constants from the Kconfig values. The `TBFT_*` macros can be overridden by defining them before including the header (`#ifndef` guards at `src/tbft_config.h:12-78`), but in practice the values come from `CONFIG_TBFT_*`.

| Constant | Formula / Value | Source line | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TBFT_DIGEST_SIZE` | `32` | `src/tbft_config.h:85` | SHA-256 output size. |
| `TBFT_HMAC_SIZE` | `32` | `src/tbft_config.h:86` | HMAC-SHA256 output size. |
| `TBFT_HMAC_KEY_SIZE` | `32` | `src/tbft_config.h:87` | Symmetric session key size. |
| `TBFT_RSA_KEY_BITS` | `2048` | `src/tbft_config.h:88` | RSA key size (slow path). |
| `TBFT_SIG_SIZE` | `TBFT_RSA_KEY_BITS / 8` = 256 | `src/tbft_config.h:89` | RSA signature size. |
| `TBFT_AUTH_SIZE` | `TBFT_HMAC_SIZE × (TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS - 1)` | `src/tbft_config.h:92` | Authenticator array: one HMAC slot per remote replica. |
| `TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS` | `TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE / TBFT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL + 2` | `src/tbft_config.h:95` | Checkpoint log slots (window/interval + 2 for overlap). |
| `TBFT_MAX_FAULTY` | `(TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS - 1) / 3` | `src/tbft_config.h:98` | Maximum `f` at compile time (sizing). |
| `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS` | `TBFT_MAX_FAULTY + 1` | `src/tbft_config.h:101` | Max distinct values stored per certificate. |
| `TBFT_P_CHILDREN` | `(TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE - 40) / (TBFT_DIGEST_SIZE + sizeof(int32_t))` | `src/tbft_config.h:104-105` | Children per partition-tree node. |
| `TBFT_ANTI_REPLAY_WINDOW_US` | `CONFIG_TBFT_ANTI_REPLAY_WINDOW_MS × 1000` | `src/tbft_config.h:57` | Anti-replay window in microseconds. |
| `TBFT_VIEW_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_US` | `CONFIG_TBFT_VIEW_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_US` | `src/tbft_config.h:61` | View-change period in microseconds. |
| `TBFT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_US` | `CONFIG_TBFT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_US` | `src/tbft_config.h:65` | Status broadcast period in microseconds. |
| `TBFT_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_US` | `CONFIG_TBFT_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT_US` (defaults 2500000) | `src/tbft_config.h:68-74` | State fetch / recovery period. |
| `TBFT_CLIENT_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `CONFIG_TBFT_CLIENT_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `src/tbft_config.h:77` | Client reply-collection timeout. |

A worked example for the `counter` deployment (`MAX_NUM_REPLICAS=7`, `WINDOW_SIZE=4`, `CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL=2`, `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE=2048`, `BLOCK_SIZE=1024`):

| Constant | Computation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `TBFT_AUTH_SIZE` | `32 × (7-1)` | 192 bytes |
| `TBFT_NUM_CKPT_SLOTS` | `4 / 2 + 2` | 4 slots |
| `TBFT_MAX_FAULTY` | `(7-1) / 3` | 2 |
| `TBFT_CERT_MAX_VALS` | `2 + 1` | 3 distinct values |
| `TBFT_P_CHILDREN` | `(2048 - 40) / (32 + 4)` | 55 children |

`memcalc.sh` (`examples/counter/memcalc.sh:18-24`) computes the same values in shell for the static-size estimate. The `New_key` message size is constrained by `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`:

```text
New_key_bytes = 24 (rep hdr) + (n-1) × 260 (per-replica slot) + 256 (RSA sig)
              = 24 + 6×260 + 256
              = 1840 bytes
```

`out_buf` (sized to `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`) must be ≥ this. The `counter` deployment uses `2048` (`examples/counter/sdkconfig.defaults:23`) which leaves 208 bytes of slack.

## Compile-time assertions

`src/tbft_config.h:111-143` enforces these invariants at every build. Each is a `_Static_assert` that fails the compilation with a clear message if violated.

| Assertion | Source line | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `TBFT_BLOCK_SIZE` is a positive power of 2 | `src/tbft_config.h:111-113` | Non-power-of-2 block size in `sdkconfig` |
| `TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE > TBFT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL` | `src/tbft_config.h:115-116` | Window too small to hold the checkpoint interval |
| `TBFT_WINDOW_SIZE` is a positive power of 2 | `src/tbft_config.h:118-120` | Non-power-of-2 window |
| `TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS >= 4` | `src/tbft_config.h:122-123` | BFT requires `n = 3f+1`, so at least 4 replicas |
| `TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS <= 64` | `src/tbft_config.h:125-128` | `tbft_bitmap_t` is `uint64_t`; > 64 silently drops senders and allows Byzantine re-voting |
| `TBFT_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL >= 1` | `src/tbft_config.h:130-131` | Prevents divide-by-zero in `slot_index` |
| `TBFT_MAX_REPLY_SIZE < TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` | `src/tbft_config.h:133-134` | Reply must fit inside the message envelope |
| `TBFT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE % 8 == 0` | `src/tbft_config.h:136-137` | Avoids stack-buffer overflow in message alignment padding |
| `TBFT_P_CHILDREN > 0` | `src/tbft_config.h:139-140` | `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE` too small for the partition tree |
| `TBFT_P_LEVELS >= 2` | `src/tbft_config.h:142-143` | At least 2 levels for the Merkle tree |

The 64-replica cap is the most important one to be aware of: the message bitmap is a single `uint64_t` (`tbft_bitmap_t`), so trying to scale above 64 replicas would silently no-op `tbft_bitmap_set` / `tbft_bitmap_test` and let a Byzantine replica vote multiple times. The Kconfig `range 4 32` prevents this from happening accidentally.

## Config file format

The config file is parsed by `parse_config()` in `src/tbft_libbyz.c:96`. It is plain UTF-8 text, line-based, with one `fscanf`-read token per field. The full layout (with line numbers referencing the parser):

| Line | Content | Parser source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `<service_name>` (≤63 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:107` — `%63s` |
| 2 | `<f>` — number of tolerated faults (1..`TBFT_MAX_FAULTY`) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:108,114-118` |
| 3 | `<auth_timeout_ms>` — request authentication timeout (ms, > 0) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:109,216-220` |
| 4 | `<num_nodes>` — total entries (replicas + clients) (≥ `3f+1`, ≤ `MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + MAX_NUM_CLIENTS`) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:110,121-132` |
| 5 | `<multicast_ip>` — IPv4 dotted-quad (≤31 chars); ignored when `TBFT_DISABLE_MULTICAST=y` | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:111` |
| 6 .. `5+num_nodes` | One node line per entry (format depends on transport — see below) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:134-187` |
| `6+num_nodes` | `<view_change_timeout_ms>` (> 0) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:212,216-220` |
| `7+num_nodes` | `<status_timeout_ms>` (> 0) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:213,216-220` |
| `8+num_nodes` | `<recovery_timeout_ms>` (> 0) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:214,216-220` |

The example deployment `examples/counter/spiffs_image/config_espnow.txt` (generated by `examples/counter/gen_configs.sh:36-53`) looks like:

```text
counter                # line  1: service name
2                      # line  2: f (max tolerated faults)
60000                  # line  3: auth timeout (ms)
8                      # line  4: num_nodes (7 replicas + 1 client)
0.0.0.0                # line  5: multicast IP (ignored for ESP-NOW)
node0 88:56:a6:5b:f2:f0 /spiffs/pub0.der    # line  6
node1 88:56:a6:5b:76:84 /spiffs/pub1.der    # line  7
node2 1c:db:d4:c6:40:98 /spiffs/pub2.der    # line  8
node3 1c:db:d4:c5:7f:20 /spiffs/pub3.der    # line  9
node4 1c:db:d4:c6:40:40 /spiffs/pub4.der    # line 10
node5 88:56:a6:5b:6b:2c /spiffs/pub5.der    # line 11
node6 88:56:a6:5b:78:dc /spiffs/pub6.der    # line 12
client7 e8:3d:c1:8c:18:58 /spiffs/pub7.der  # line 13
60000                  # line 14: view_change timeout (ms)
5000                   # line 15: status timeout (ms)
10000                  # line 16: recovery timeout (ms)
```

The `simple_wallet` example produces a 4-node file (`examples/simple_wallet/gen_configs.sh:32-45`) with `f=1`, `num_nodes=4`, and a shorter layout. The hostname prefix decides replica vs client:

| Hostname starts with | Counts as | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `node` | Replica | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:192-193` (`strncmp("node", 4) == 0`) |
| anything else (e.g. `client7`) | Client | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:192-198` (counter — `num_replicas++` only on `node*`) |

The total `num_replicas` must be at least 1 (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:195-198`) and at most `TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:205-210`). If `num_replicas < 3f+1` the parser logs a warning and computes a reduced effective fault tolerance:

```text
W (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: num_replicas=4 < 3f+1=4: reduced fault tolerance
                     (max tolerated faults with 4 replicas = 1)
```

(`src/tbft_libbyz.c:200-204`)

## UDP mode node line format

When `CONFIG_TBFT_TRANSPORT_UDP=y`, each node line has four whitespace-separated fields:

```text
<hostname> <ip> <port> <pubkey_path>
```

| Field | Type | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hostname` | string (≤63 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:138` (`%63s`) | Used to detect replicas (`node*` prefix). |
| `ip` | IPv4 dotted-quad (≤31 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:138,174` (`%31s`) | Validated by `inet_pton` in `setup_principals()` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:362-369`). |
| `port` | integer 1..65535 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:176,181-185` | Stored network-order via `htons` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:371`). |
| `pubkey_path` | string (≤127 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:176` (`%127s`) | SPIFFS path to the DER public key, e.g. `/spiffs/pub0.der`. |

A UDP node line is recognised by the absence of `:` in the second field (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:143` — `is_mac = strchr(field2, ':')`). If a `:` is present and the compiled transport is UDP, the parser aborts with:

```text
E (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: node 0 has MAC address but transport is UDP —
                    use a UDP config file (<hostname> <ip> <port> <pubkey>)
```

(`src/tbft_libbyz.c:147-151`)

Example lines from `examples/counter/spiffs_image/config_udp.txt` (`examples/counter/gen_configs.sh:22-29`):

```text
node0 192.168.100.109 5000 /spiffs/pub0.der
node1 192.168.100.107 5000 /spiffs/pub1.der
node2 192.168.100.106 5000 /spiffs/pub2.der
node3 192.168.100.104 5000 /spiffs/pub3.der
node4 192.168.100.108 5000 /spiffs/pub4.der
node5 192.168.100.105 5000 /spiffs/pub5.der
node6 192.168.100.194 5000 /spiffs/pub6.der
client7 192.168.100.190 5000 /spiffs/pub7.der
```

The example uses 192.168.100.0/24 and port 5000 for every node. Real deployments should assign distinct IPs (or at least distinct ports on the same host for testing) and replace the placeholder IPs with the real ones before flashing.

## ESP-NOW mode node line format

When `CONFIG_TBFT_TRANSPORT_ESPNOW=y`, each node line has three whitespace-separated fields:

```text
<hostname> <mac_address> <pubkey_path>
```

| Field | Type | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hostname` | string (≤63 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:138` (`%63s`) | Used to detect replicas (`node*` prefix). |
| `mac_address` | `xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx` (≤31 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:138,164` (`%31s`) | Parsed by `sscanf("%x:%x:...:x", ...)` in `setup_principals()` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:351-360`). Must be the **base (eFuse) MAC**, not the AP MAC — the transport applies `get_ap_mac()` internally. |
| `pubkey_path` | string (≤127 chars) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:165` (`%127s`) | SPIFFS path to the DER public key, e.g. `/spiffs/pub0.der`. |

The `mac_address` field is recognised by the presence of `:` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:143`). If it is missing and the compiled transport is ESP-NOW, the parser aborts with:

```text
E (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: node 0 has IP address but transport is ESP-NOW —
                    use an ESP-NOW config file (<hostname> <mac> <pubkey>)
```

(`src/tbft_libbyz.c:153-157`)

Example lines from `examples/counter/spiffs_image/config_espnow.txt` (`examples/counter/gen_configs.sh:42-49`):

```text
node0 88:56:a6:5b:f2:f0 /spiffs/pub0.der
node1 88:56:a6:5b:76:84 /spiffs/pub1.der
node2 1c:db:d4:c6:40:98 /spiffs/pub2.der
node3 1c:db:d4:c5:7f:20 /spiffs/pub3.der
node4 1c:db:d4:c6:40:40 /spiffs/pub4.der
node5 88:56:a6:5b:6b:2c /spiffs/pub5.der
node6 88:56:a6:5b:78:dc /spiffs/pub6.der
client7 e8:3d:c1:8c:18:58 /spiffs/pub7.der
```

`local_node_id` is auto-detected at `Byz_init_replica` time by matching the eFuse MAC against the config entries (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:226-262`). A case-insensitive compare handles upper- or lower-case hex digits in the config file. If no match is found, the parser logs a warning:

```text
W (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: local MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff not found in config —
                     ensure config contains base (eFuse) MACs, not AP MACs
```

(`src/tbft_libbyz.c:256-260`)

For UDP, the auto-detection uses the WiFi STA interface IP (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:264-289`); it requires the WiFi connection to be established before `Byz_init_replica` is called.

## Private key path

The local node's RSA-2048 private key is **not** part of the cluster config file. It is passed as a separate path argument to `Byz_init_replica()` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:874-880`) or `Byz_init_client()` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:476-477`). The path is the same SPIFFS scheme as the public keys:

```c
Byz_init_replica("/spiffs/config_espnow.txt",   // cluster config
                 "/spiffs/priv0.der",           // local private key (DER)
                 0,                              // local_id (or -1 for auto)
                 app_state, sizeof(app_state),  // state memory
                 exec_cb,                        // app-specific exec callback
                 comp_ndet_cb, 0,                // optional non-determinism cb
                 recv_reply_cb,                  // optional reply observer
                 0);                             // bind port (0 = use config)
```

`src/tbft_libbyz.c:415-456` shows the loading and validation path. After loading, the component performs a **keypair self-test** by signing `"keypair_self_test"` with the private key and verifying with the public key (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:441-455`). A mismatch aborts init with:

```text
E (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: key pair mismatch for node 0:
                   public and private keys do not correspond
```

The private key is zeroised with `mbedtls_platform_zeroize` (`src/tbft_libbyz.c:420`) after the PSA key import — the DER buffer is freed and the bytes are wiped from the heap. The PSA key handle is retained inside `tbft_principal_t` and used for `New_key` encryption and slow-path signing.

## Parsing edge cases

A summary of the validation checks the parser performs, with the source-line references:

| Edge case | Behaviour | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Config file not found | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:98-102` |
| `f < 1` or `f > TBFT_MAX_FAULTY` | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 (suggests increasing `TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS`) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:114-118` |
| `num_nodes < 3f+1` | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:121-125` |
| `num_nodes > TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS + TBFT_MAX_NUM_CLIENTS` | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:126-132` |
| Node line with `:` and transport is UDP | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:147-151` |
| Node line without `:` and transport is ESP-NOW | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:153-157` |
| UDP port out of range [1, 65535] | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:181-184` |
| Zero replicas (`num_replicas < 1`) | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:195-198` |
| `num_replicas > TBFT_MAX_NUM_REPLICAS` | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:205-210` |
| `num_replicas < 3f+1` (but > 0) | `ESP_LOGW` — reduced effective fault tolerance | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:199-204` |
| Non-positive timeouts | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:216-220` |
| UDP node IP fails `inet_pton` | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 (in `setup_principals`) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:362-369` |
| Public-key file missing or unreadable | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 (cascading cleanup of prior principals) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:378-407` |
| Public-key DER parse failure | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:392-407` |
| Private-key DER parse failure | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:419-433` |
| Private/public key pair mismatch | `ESP_LOGE` + return -1 (keypair self-test) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:441-455` |
| Local MAC (ESP-NOW) not in config | `ESP_LOGW` (auto-detect fails, caller must supply `local_id` explicitly) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:256-260, 886-894` |
| Local IP (UDP) not in config | `ESP_LOGW` (auto-detect fails) | `src/tbft_libbyz.c:284-286` |

The cascading-cleanup pattern at `src/tbft_libbyz.c:332-341`, `:382-390`, `:398-406`, `:425-432`, `:461-467` is worth noting: when an error occurs while populating principal `i`, every previously-allocated principal `0..i-1` is freed and zeroed in `node->principals[]` before the function returns -1. This prevents a partial-init leak when the first invalid entry in a config file is hit halfway through the loop.

When `parse_config` returns 0, the parser logs a one-line summary at `INFO` level:

```text
I (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: parsed config: service=counter f=2 nodes=8 mcast=0.0.0.0
```

(`src/tbft_libbyz.c:223-224`)

The auto-detected `local_node_id` is logged on a separate line:

```text
I (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: auto-detected local_node_id=0 (MAC=88:56:a6:5b:f2:f0)
```

or, for UDP:

```text
I (NNNN) tbft_libbyz: auto-detected local_node_id=0 (IP=192.168.100.109)
```
